gen-dafont-good-times-satoshi: Satoshi stays wide and easygoing in sans-serif form. Good Times is the one to shout with, its geometric heft built for big moments, while Satoshi does its best work quietly, drawn like thin wire with tall lowercase.
gen-dafont-good-times-switzer: Wide, cable-thick geometric letters make Good Times instantly commanding. It earns its keep when set big and brief, while Switzer hums along beneath in tall, wire-like sans-serif forms.
gen-dafont-groovy-bitter: Bitter is a slab-serif with a huge lowercase and gaps you can see through. Under Groovy's nearly shut, loosely tracked letters it reads openly and steadily, like a sturdy table after a funky party.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noticia-text: Literary and dignified, Noticia Text reads with wide entrances into its curves and lowercase bodies that fill most of the line height. Groovy's friendly, funky slits are its foil.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-pridi: Refined, with generous gaps where curves meet stems, Pridi stands proud as a serif whose small letters nearly match capitals in height. Groovy's bent-cable lines are the foil.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-scope-one: Scope One is a text serif with a big x-height and stubby ascenders. Groovy is the loud, friendly one, drawn at a single stroke width, while Scope One quietly handles the sentences with counters that spill open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-suwannaphum: Groovy's narrow, almost-closed slit in the c gives it a funky, friendly face, with no brush-like swelling anywhere. Then Suwannaphum, a dignified serif with a high, squared-off x-height and a c open like a bent paperclip, takes over the reading.
gen-dafont-groovy-rubik: Friendly and funky, Groovy squeezes its c almost shut and spaces its lowercase loosely. Rubik answers with soft, open round letters and a big lowercase that stay legible at small sizes.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-fs-bespoke-sans: Authoritative, flat-lined Hammerhead looks like fineliner on paper, its wide-open e never squeezed shut, and it hits hardest at display size. But Bespoke Sans is the sharper, finer reader, giving curve ends plenty of room.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-gf-kiwi-maru: Hammerhead is plain, unmodulated outline with an open e. It makes the bold statement, while Kiwi Maru, a serif with generous letterspace and far-reaching terminals, carries the editorial reading.
